body_text:
Is this email difficult to read? View it in a web browser. › https://wealthadviser.cmail20.com/t/d-e-wjrdjhy-tjitdkjtyk-f/

                 

Rebecca Noble/Bloomberg News



At Labor Day picnics this year, millions fewer Americans could brag about having a sub-3% mortgage than a few years ago.

That might be a relief for frustrated home buyers sick of hearing about it.  But it is an ominous sign for investors [https://www.wsj.com/finance/why-mortgage-bonds-are-at-risk-if-rates-riseand-if-they-fall-ff897dd5].

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

Planning & Investing               Malls Were Left for Dead. Now They Are the Top Performer in Commercial Real Estate

Mall values jumped [https://www.wsj.com/real-estate/commercial/malls-were-left-for-dead-now-they-are-the-top-performer-in-commercial-real-estate-0bf6100f] 13% in a year, more than doubling commercial-property price gains.

Market Talk               

From  Dow Jones Newswires [https://www.dowjones.com/professional/newswires/]



Royal Bank of Canada chief economist Frances Donald and her team say they are cautiously optimistic about the Canadian outlook despite uncertainty swirling about US-Canada trade. She forecasts sub-2% growth this year and next but argues the economy is stronger on a per-capita basis amid stalled population growth. The commodity-rich provinces in western Canada are leading the charge on growth. RBC expects four Bank of Canada rate hikes next year, taking the policy rate to 3.25%, due to concern over higher energy prices and an improving economy. Still, Donald adds "there are growing risks that [the] first hike could come" later in 2026. (Paul Vieira, Paul.Vieira@wsj.com)

A slowdown in the development of artificial-intelligence models brings credit risk into the AI market narrative, Swissquote's Ipek Ozkardeskaya writes. Long-term financial commitments for data-center capacity and power could come under strain if the demand for such infrastructure isn't as high as anticipated, the analyst says. "If the AI race slows materially, the key question becomes: who pays for all that infrastructure?" Ozkardeskaya writes. "The leases, debt and power commitments remain even if expected compute demand and revenue growth slow." AI's central role in driving stocks higher and boosting productivity leaves markets vulnerable to any downturn in sentiment, Ozkardeskaya adds. (Joe Stonor, josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)

Barron's Advisor               A Top Advisor to Dentists, Professors, and Other Niche Clients

Savant Wealth Management sets itself apart by  knowing what very specific types of clients need [https://www.barrons.com/advisor/articles/advisor-dentists-professors-clients-7c104752]—and then delivering it.

For Ultrawealthy Clients, a Host of Services Under One Roof

How the Mather Group, a Barron’s top-ranked RIA, uses acquisitions to cater to  ultrahigh-net-worth families [https://www.barrons.com/advisor/articles/advisor-ultrawealthy-clients-9e00c4fd].

Business & Practice               How the Clash Between Money and Safety Created a Monumental Crisis for AI

OpenAI and Anthropic, in heated competition—with each other and China—are racing toward IPOs, even as they admit they  could lose control of their powerful bots [https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-anthropic-crisis-money-safety-847bc1d6].

Impact Investing               Wealthy Europeans Are Moving North as Temperatures Climb

Regions of northern Spain, France and Italy become more attractive  for buyers [https://www.wsj.com/world/europe/wealthy-europeans-are-moving-north-as-temperatures-climb-9b47dac0] as wildfires and droughts hit southern hot spots.

Talking Points               Here’s What It’s Like to Retire to a Low-Tax State

Many Americans dream of relocating in retirement to stretch their nest eggs, and they often do it by  moving to low-tax states [https://www.wsj.com/personal-finance/heres-what-its-like-to-retire-to-a-low-tax-state-fcac6598].

Travel & Lifestyle               At Restaurants, Phones Are Becoming the New Cigarettes            

Elizabeth Arvelos Coetzee/Alexandra Citrin-Safadi/WSJ



Screen-time while dining is now as taboo as smoking. Here’s how you can  kick the habit [https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/food-cooking/at-restaurants-phones-are-becoming-the-new-cigarettes-689c6435].

Has Your Accent Just Become a Security Vulnerability?

New research suggests that when a scammer uses AI to sound just like you, you are  more likely to fall prey [https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/accent-ai-voice-security-96154f75] to the scam.
